title: Two SPHEREx reductions retain the 2025 3.1 um band of Gaia20cdd; evidence in July 2026 depends on the continuum
abstract: We test the reported 3.1 um band of Gaia20cdd with two published SPHEREx photometry reductions. The four 2025 in-band fluxes agree to within 4.3 percent. With a Gaussian profile and a quadratic local continuum, the two-visit ice reduction gives a peak depth of 0.380 +/- 0.055. A second reduction contains later band coverage on 2026 July 21-22. This third visit gives depth 0.290 +/- 0.054 with a linear continuum, but 0.221 +/- 0.084 with a quadratic continuum. Deleting one exposure can reduce the latter formal amplitude statistic below one. A control star has a large false-looking band from one near-zero flux, which shows why formal significance alone is insufficient. The 2025 feature survives an extraction-method and continuum test. The July 2026 feature gives tentative evidence for recurrence over one year. Shared images and calibration prevent an independent detection claim. This audit does not confirm water ice or measure a grain lifetime. We preserve reproducible code, input hashes, control tests, simulations and fit results.
